title: Other Asset Classes
source: Lecture8_MGT595_2023.pptx (103 slides, markitdown extraction; tables mostly images, several charts have embedded data)

Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), 'Time Series Momentum', JFE

page_groups.content: Title; overview: Value and Momentum 'everywhere'; No momentum in Japan? So what?; Time-Series Momentum; Sports betting (if time permits); implications for EMH.

AMP motivation: value and momentum usually studied separately, one asset class at a time; literature had nothing on gov bonds or value in commodities/currencies. What we do: unified measures, all classes simultaneously; combining classes and combining value WITH momentum gives large economic and statistical gains; test common explanations (macro, liquidity risk).

Main results: V&M positive Sharpe in ALL major classes despite negative correlation; 50/50 combo beats either; large diversification benefits; striking co-movement: value here correlates with value there, momentum ditto, V-M negatively correlated everywhere. Macro risk explains little. Liquidity risk: VALUE LOADS POSITIVELY and MOMENTUM NEGATIVELY on funding-liquidity risk (notes: t-stats -3.2 and +3.8 once noise is diversified away); partly explains comovement and the negative V-M correlation, but makes momentum MORE puzzling. Dynamics: liquidity risk importance rises sharply after summer 1998; over time both become less profitable, more correlated across markets and with each other. Only visible looking everywhere.

Data: stocks US/UK/Japan/Europe (top ~37.5% of caps = 96-98% of market cap), country indices (MSCI), bonds (10yr MSCI/Datastream), currencies, 27 commodities by exchange. Measures: MOMENTUM = return t-12 to t-2 EVERYWHERE. VALUE: stocks book-to-price; indices aggregate B/P; commodities 'book' = avg spot price 4.5-5.5 years ago; currencies 5yr excess-return reversal (deviation from UIP / PPP change); bonds real yield = yield minus expected inflation. Methodology: terciles, value-weight stocks / equal-weight others, 50/50 combos, H-L spreads; robustness equal-vol weighting (commodities have ~5x the vol of bonds).

Table I & II and Figures (IMAGES - numbers not extracted): performance across 8 markets/classes; notes say ubiquitous positive returns, big negative V-M correlation within classes, combo higher SR and more stable, long-short split uninteresting; Japan momentum weakness clarified (value strong there, combo fine, and weak momentum is what you'd expect given negative correlation with a strong value run - the famous Asness Japan point in the overview line 'No momentum in Japan? So what?'). Figure 1 PC analysis: first PC separates value vs momentum globally; Figure 5: V&M in one market explained by V&M in OTHER markets; Figure 6 asset pricing tests: 48 global V&M portfolios priced better by global 3-factor (market + everywhere-value + everywhere-momentum) than by local models.

Power of looking everywhere: liquidity risk t-stats -3.2 (momentum... note says value +, momentum -) and 3.8 once noise diversified. Notes: 'cheap assets get cheaper during liquidity events, but trending assets do better.' Conclusions: theory must accommodate large combined Sharpes and cross-class links.

TSMOM title and definitions: TIME SERIES momentum = a security's OWN past return predicts its future return, vs CROSS-SECTIONAL = relative outperformance predicts relative outperformance. Most direct test of random walk; behavioral and rational theories are about absolute returns. 2x2 literature table: autocorrelation (FF 1988, Lo-MacKinlay 1988) = n-months-predict-n-months time series; standard momentum (JT) = m-predict-n cross-sectional; MOP fills m-predict-n time series. Data: 58 liquid futures (24 commodities, 12 currency pairs eventually, 9 equity indices, 13 bond futures).

Regression evidence (IMAGES): panel regressions of scaled return on lagged scaled returns; sign predictability up to 12 months positive, reverses beyond. Strategy: BUY if past-12-month excess return positive, SHORT if negative; scale positions to equal ex-ante vol; 12M TSMOM Sharpe by instrument (image).

EMBEDDED CHART DATA (REAL, AQR 1880-2017 trend-following gross Sharpe by asset): equities e.g. Australia ASX 0.86, Canada 0.55, Spain 0.68, Japan Topix 0.46, S&P500 0.41, FTSE 0.21; bonds e.g. Germany 5yr 1.02, Germany 10yr 0.85, Italy 10yr 0.73, US 10yr 0.67, US 5yr 0.64, Australia 3yr 0.06; FX e.g. USDJPY 0.60, USDGBP 0.56, AUDNZD 0.08; commodities e.g. Brent 0.59, GasOil 0.60, Zinc 0.50, Cotton 0.47, Crude 0.45, Sugar 0.43, Gold 0.33, Cocoa 0.08, Coffee 0.12. Nearly all 66 positive.

Diversified TSMOM: trade 12M strategy across all 58 instruments; ~9-10% annualized vol; realistic margin use (5-20%). Large alpha to standard factors (image). Robust across look-back/holding grids in every class (image). Large intercepts relative to CROSS-SECTIONAL momentum factors (AMP): TSMOM subsumes XSMOM but not vice versa. Lo-MacKinlay/Lewellen decomposition: XSMOM = autocovariance + cross-covariance + mean dispersion; TSMOM = autocovariance + mean-squared; AUTO-COVARIANCE (own past return predicting own future) explains MOST of both - they are close cousins and the driver is the same.

Not transaction costs (performance unrelated to liquidity in TS or XS). Not crash risk: TSMOM does WELL in extreme markets - the 'smile': regressing TSMOM on market return and squared market return gives positive convexity. EMBEDDED CHART DATA (REAL): 10 largest 60/40 drawdowns 1880-2015 with trend-following net-of-2/20 returns: Feb-Aug 1893: -12.3% vs +8.6%; Oct1906-Dec1907: -16.8% vs +26.5%; Dec1916-Dec1917: -12.1% vs +25.6%; Sep1929-Jun1932: -62.3% vs +36.1%; Mar1937-Mar1938: -32.5% vs -8.1%; Dec1968-Jun1970: -19.9% vs +54.8%; Jan1973-Sep1974: -30.6% vs +95.4%; Sep-Nov 1987: -18.0% vs -2.4%; Sep2000-Sep2002: -21.2% vs +26.4%; Nov2007-Feb2009: -30.5% vs +21.6%. Trend positive in 8 of the 10 worst 60/40 episodes ('crisis alpha').

Mechanism: who trades - SPECULATORS are positioned WITH the trend, HEDGERS against (speculators long TSMOM, hedgers short). Event study / impulse response: price continues for ~12 months then partially REVERSES - consistent with initial under-reaction AND delayed over-reaction. Splitting futures return = spot price change + roll return: price-change component drives continuation then reverses (over-reaction present); roll-return component (hedging pressure via futures-curve shape) is PERSISTENT and does not reverse. Both spot changes, roll returns, and CFTC speculator positions predict returns. Conclusion: 'A Trending Walk Down Wall Street.'

Sports betting laboratory: motivation - financial markets can't separate risk vs behavioral vs data-mining cleanly (joint hypothesis, unobservable preferences). Betting markets: IDIOSYNCRATIC bets (no systematic risk premium justified) and FINITE TERMINAL DATE where uncertainty resolves via outcomes UNRELATED to bettor activity - truth revealed. Market size $500B-1T (~$5B legal Vegas); SportsDirect 1999-2013 + SportsInsight 2005-2013; NBA NFL MLB NHL; opening line, closing line, outcome. Three contract types with EXACT payoff rules: SPREAD: $110 bet on A at -N points pays 210 if margin > N, 110 push, 0 fail (the 'vig' = 10% difference); MONEYLINE: $100 on A listed -$M pays M+100 win; OVER/UNDER: $110 on total > T pays 210. Returns split: open-to-close (line movement) vs close-to-end (outcome). Sentiment should NOT predict outcome; information SHOULD.

Framework and hypotheses: regress open-to-close and close-to-end returns on characteristics: H1 no relevance beta1=betaT=0; H2 efficiency: line moves ARE information (beta1 != 0 and betaT confirms); H3 pure noise/total overreaction: beta1 != 0, betaT = -beta1 (full reversal); H4 inefficiency: Cov(beta1,betaT)<0 overreaction, >0 underreaction. Momentum measures analogous to finance: past game payoffs / win% / score differentials (composites, avg corr 0.55-0.85). RESULTS: STRONG momentum in line movement open-to-close that is COMPLETELY REVERSED by game end - overreaction/mispricing, replicated in BetFair data.

Value measures (long-term past performance, payroll/spread, E(P)/P from win-probability models; avg corr 0.32): WEAKER value effects, also reversed. Size (franchise value, revenue): NO effect. Survey validation: Fama - 'Most of these make sense to me... past team record longer-term for value, shorter-term for momentum'; Thaler - 'Momentum is easier. For value, since that's my measure with DeBondt, I guess I have to like that one.' Magnitudes: effects in betting markets are ~1/5 the size of financial-market analogs; profits easily wiped out by the vig; NO covariance structure across contracts sharing characteristics (unlike financial factors - so no risk-based story is even possible, and none is needed given full reversal). Uncertainty interaction fits overreaction theory (DHS 1998, Rabin 2002): momentum STRONGER early in season/with more uncertainty, value stronger with less; SAME pattern found in US equities. Conclusion: clear mispricing; limits to arbitrage (the vig) prevent correction; generalization to financial markets is suggestive but magnitudes much smaller and structures differ.

gap_analysis: Most AMP tables (Table I performance numbers, Table II correlations) are images; the app uses the paper's qualitative structure plus the deck's own note statements (t-stats -3.2/+3.8 for liquidity loadings, negative V-M correlation, combo dominance) and avoids invented per-class Sharpe values; the results visual is labeled stylized where exact.

TSMOM 'scale to ex-ante annualized volatility 0.60%' in extraction is a mangled fragment; the paper's standard is 40%/sigma position scaling - the app's problem uses the 40%/sigma convention and labels it as the paper's.
The two embedded chart datasets (66-asset trend Sharpes 1880-2017; ten 60/40 drawdowns vs trend) are used EXACTLY as extracted.

Sports betting result tables are images; the app presents the hypothesis framework, payoff rules (fully specified in text), the 1/5-magnitude statement, full-reversal finding, and quotes, all stated in deck text.
